purpose: G1 ready-button native-boundary test and correction of the room command callbacks

runs.name: codex-1649370-ready-hit-20261021
runs.purpose: verify that the corrected GFx dispatch breakpoints execute and that the old scanner operand addresses were mid-instruction
runs.observation: Both corrected GFx dispatch sites hit once during UI page initialization, before any room action. The previous probes had armed 0x7D0A43/0x7D08C3, which are immediate operand bytes, so their zero-hit results did not cover these dispatches.

runs.name: codex-1649370-ready-native2-20261021
runs.purpose: check whether a human click on Ready reaches the native ready-message or room-start entries
ui_actions: human entered the local room through the custom-game UI
human clicked the visible Ready button at the bottom-right; the human confirmed the click was on the correct control
runs.observed_result: The Ready button did not change text or colour. None of the three native breakpoints hit.
runs.interpretation: The Ready control is inert in the offline local room: the click did not reach the native ready-message builder or the room-start command. This is consistent with the earlier ABC finding that CFunctionContainer.SetReadyState is an empty stub in the shipped movie; it does not prove every possible native binding is absent, but it removes the 'our synthetic click missed the button' explanation.
runs.stop_cause: an explicit out-of-process experiment called room.startgame (0x6398A0) from a newly created thread; the engine rejected the non-main-thread call with Com Error and the probe recorded an access violation at 0x773752

room_commands.previous_error: 0x639890 had been labelled the room.startgame handler; it is the room.leave dispatch

conclusion: G1 is now narrowed to an inert Ready control in the offline room. A human click produces no UI state change and no hit at the native ready-message builder or the start command. The next experiment must bypass the Ready control on the game's main thread, not synthesize another click. 0x6398A0 is the real room.startgame callback; 0x639890 is room.leave. A non-main-thread call is invalid and produced the expected engine rejection, so the next wrapper must inject a command or call on the main thread only.
